cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet of the LORD, has a word about the prophets. He says his heart is broken within him and all his bones tremble. Friend, I know that tremble, because that was me in the back of the junk drawer every single time the light came in.

cards.question: Jeremiah says he's become like a drunkard, like a man overcome by wine. What does he say has done this to him?

answers.text: The LORD and His holy words

cards.text: Then Jeremiah looks at the land, and it's full of adulterers. Because of the curse, the land mourns and the wilderness pastures have dried up, drier than the batch I forgot in the oven for an HOUR.

cards.question: Jeremiah says that in the land, power is being used the way it should be.

cards.text: Now the LORD Himself speaks. Friend, I'd hate to be the one getting looked at right now, because I'd be scooting my gold base behind the oven SO fast.

cards.question: The LORD says both prophet and ___ are ungodly, and He has found their wickedness even in His ___.

cards.text: So what's coming? Their path will become slick, the LORD says. Friend, I once hopped across a counter covered in spilled sprinkles, gold base and all, and I went DOWN.

cards.question: On that slick path, what does the LORD say happens to these prophets and priests?

answers.text: They're driven into darkness and fall
They find their way back home

cards.text: Disaster is coming in the year of their punishment, the LORD says. Then He turns to the prophets of Samaria, and what did He see there? An offensive thing.

cards.question: The prophets of Samaria prophesied by ___ and led the LORD's people Israel astray.

cards.text: Samaria's prophets got an offensive thing, but among Jerusalem's prophets the LORD says He has seen a horrible thing. Friend, that's going from "this batch is a little crispy" to "is the KITCHEN on fire?"

cards.question: What does the LORD say the prophets of Jerusalem do?

answers.text: Commit adultery and walk in lies
Bow to golden calves at Bethel
Refuse to speak His name aloud

cards.question: The prophets of Jerusalem strengthen the hands of evildoers. Because of that, people are turning their backs on wickedness.
To the LORD, these prophets are all like ___, and the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah.

cards.text: So the LORD of Hosts says He'll feed these prophets wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink. Friend, I spent YEARS lying on old takeout menus in that drawer, and not one of them had that on it.

cards.question: Why does the LORD of Hosts say this about the prophets of Jerusalem?

answers.text: Ungodliness spread from them through the land
They moved their altars out to Samaria
They stopped teaching the priests the law

cards.text: Now the LORD of Hosts has a word for the people these prophets have been prophesying to.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts tells the people to listen closely to the words of these prophets.
The LORD says these prophets are filling the people with false hopes. Where do their visions come from?

answers.text: From the priests in the temple
From the elders at the gate

cards.text: To those who despise the LORD, these prophets keep saying, "The LORD says that you will have peace," and they've got another line ready for everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart.

cards.question: What do these prophets keep telling everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart?

answers.text: No harm will come to you
Turn back while you still can
The LORD has seen your sin

cards.text: That's a smoke alarm that just yells "Everything's FINE" louder and louder. But the LORD asks which of them has stood in His council to see and hear His word, and who has given heed to His word and obeyed it.

cards.question: Then the LORD says to look: His ___ has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down on the heads of the wicked.
The LORD says His anger will turn back before He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart.

cards.text: In the days to come, the LORD says, you will understand this clearly. Friend, it's like a recipe that only makes sense once the timer goes off and the batch comes out.

cards.question: The LORD says He never ___ these prophets, yet they have run with their message.

cards.text: He didn't speak to them, yet they prophesied. That's a guy strolling into my bakery in an apron yelling "Papa SENT me!" when Papa did NOT send him.

cards.question: These prophets never stood in the LORD's council. If they had, what does He say they would have done?

answers.text: Turned His people from their evil ways
Gone off to prophesy in Samaria

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now. Hang on, friend, the LORD's not done talking about these prophets.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of Jeremiah 23 with "As for the prophets," but the opening card never says which prophets these are or who the message is for. It says only that Jeremiah "has a word about the prophets" and then uses its third sentence on a drawer joke instead of the missing context.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from verse 11 except that the LORD speaks. The rest is a joke about hiding from being "looked at," but the card never says what the LORD is looking at or saying, so the moment doesn't make sense. It also gives the baker nothing to reason from for the fill in the blank on card 6 (priest, house).

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "They're carried off to Babylon" is close to verse 12's "driven away into the darkness." A baker could argue that being driven away means exile to Babylon, which is where Jerusalem's prophets were later carried (Jeremiah 29:1).

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card uses verse 13 (the offensive thing among Samaria's prophets) as well as verse 14, but it cites only Jeremiah 23:14.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Samaria's prophets got an offensive thing" misstates verse 13. The text says the LORD saw an offensive thing among the prophets of Samaria. It does not say they received one.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "paid" is a different kind of thing from "sent" and "warned" and has a different tone. It reads as a modern, slightly silly option next to the others.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the line saying the story isn't over, and it tells no verse. It cites Jeremiah 23:22 anyway, even though verse 22 was already told on card 12.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the line saying the story isn't over and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field cite? The last verse of the passage, the verse of the choice card before it, or something else?
